metadata.goal: Analyze taxi operating patterns under different environmental and service conditions.
metadata.header: Porto Taxi Speed across Weather, Service Sources, and Time
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed set of 360 road-aligned Porto taxi trips organized into 180 dry–rain matched route comparisons. Request source, activity period, archived hourly weather, and dense GPS paths support three complementary speed analyses.

insight_list.insight: Rainy trips have lower average speeds than comparable dry trips, with the gap largest during high-activity daytime periods.

insights: Rainy trips have lower average speeds than comparable dry trips, with the gap largest during high-activity daytime periods.
Taxi-stand and call-center trips slow more in rainy periods, while street-hail trips show a smaller change in speed.
Weather-associated speed differences are larger during morning and late-afternoon high-activity periods, but become much smaller during late-night hours.
summary: Rain lowers speed across matched routes, with the strongest reductions during morning and late-afternoon high-activity periods. Taxi-stand and call-center trips exhibit larger rainy slowdowns than street-hail trips, while late-night weather differences are small.
